note: JAL economic event knowledge base. sig=1-5 typical market significance. dir: upside_surprise / downside_surprise = fundamental-based typical first-order reaction (not advice).

us_cpi.x: The main event for US inflation. Core CPI m/m is the number that matters; it moves Fed cut/hike expectations directly. A miss of even 0.1pp against consensus reprices rates, equities and the dollar.
us_cpi.u: Hot print: rate-cut expectations pared. US yields up, growth sold, dollar up and yen down. In Japan, OW value/banks and UW high-P/E growth; the weak yen helps exporters and inbound.
us_cpi.d: Cool print: cuts pulled forward. US yields down, equities up with growth leading, dollar down and yen up. In Japan, a tailwind for high-P/E growth and real estate; exporters face the strong-yen headwind.

us_core_pce.x: The inflation gauge the Fed formally targets. It lands after CPI so the surprise is usually small, but its weight jumps in the run-up to an FOMC.
us_core_pce.u: Cuts pushed out: US yields up, dollar up. Japan skews OW banks, UW growth.
us_core_pce.d: Cuts pulled forward: yields down, equities up. Japan skews OW growth and quality.

us_nfp.x: First Friday of the month: payrolls, the unemployment rate and average hourly earnings in one release. Because it reads on both growth and wage inflation, equities, rates and FX all move together.
us_nfp.u: Strong jobs: growth reassuring but cuts pushed out. Yields up, dollar up, and equities often trade good-news-is-bad-news. For Japan, the weaker yen argues OW exporters and higher yields OW banks.
us_nfp.d: Weak jobs: cuts pulled forward but growth doubts. Yields down, dollar down, yen up. A sharp miss turns it into a recession trade and sells everything, leaving Japan OW defensives (telecom, food, pharma).

us_unemp.x: Released alongside payrolls. Once the Sahm rule (3-month average 0.5pp above its 12-month low) comes into play, the recession trade catches fire.
us_unemp.u: Unemployment up: cuts pulled forward but recession risk rises. In Japan, OW defensives and quality, UW cyclicals.
us_unemp.d: Unemployment down: growth resilient. OW Japanese cyclicals, and higher yields put banks on the OW side.

us_ism_mfg.x: Month-start manufacturing survey; 50 divides expansion from contraction. New orders and the prices sub-index carry the lead information. A proxy for the global manufacturing cycle.
us_ism_mfg.u: Manufacturing recovering: OW cyclicals such as materials, machinery and semis. A tailwind for Japan's cyclicals - machinery, chemicals, steel.
us_ism_mfg.d: A deeper move below 50: UW cyclicals, OW defensives. A headwind for Japan's capex-linked names.

us_ism_svc.x: Survey of the services sector, roughly 70% of the US economy. The employment and prices sub-indices are also read as inflation data.
us_ism_svc.u: Services firm: US domestic demand strong and yields biased higher, which with a softer yen supports Japanese exporters and banks.
us_ism_svc.d: Services stalling: US growth worries push yields down and the yen up - a headwind for Japanese exporters.

us_retail.x: The monthly read on US consumption. The control group, the part that feeds GDP, is what matters. US consumption is the last line of defense for global growth.
us_retail.u: Strong consumer: OW cyclicals and consumption plays; higher yields are a headwind for high-P/E growth in Japan.
us_retail.d: Consumption stalling: recession fears. OW defensives and UW Japanese companies with high US sales exposure, autos in particular.

us_gdp.x: Annualized quarterly growth. Attention fades from advance to second to third estimate. The consumption and core PCE price components are the detail that matters.
us_gdp.u: Growth beat: risk-on and yields up. OW Japanese cyclicals.
us_gdp.d: Negative growth: the recession debate opens. OW defensives in Japan, though lower yields can support real estate.

us_fomc.x: Eight meetings a year. The focus is the policy rate, the quarterly dot plot and the Powell press conference. Markets trade the forward guidance far more than the decision itself.
us_fomc.u: Hawkish surprise (a hike, or a signal that cuts are off): yields up, dollar up, equities down. Japan OW banks and UW growth, with exporters relatively resilient on the weaker yen.
us_fomc.d: Dovish surprise (faster cuts signaled): yields down, dollar down, yen up, equities up. Japan OW growth and real estate, but watch the strong-yen headwind for exporters.

us_fomc_minutes.x: Published three weeks after the meeting. A check on the nuance of the discussion; rarely a big mover alone, but it fine-tunes the hawkish/dovish temperature.
us_fomc_minutes.u: Hawkish tone: yields up, dollar up - Japanese banks over growth.
us_fomc_minutes.d: Dovish tone: yields down, equities up - Japanese growth and real estate lead.

us_ppi.x: Upstream inflation. The components that feed straight into PCE, such as healthcare and freight, get the attention. Arriving after CPI, it carries little fresh information.
us_ppi.u: Upstream inflation: margin-squeeze concerns. Japanese names with pricing power outperform.
us_ppi.d: Upstream disinflation: scope for Japanese margins to improve.

us_jolts.x: A leading indicator of labor-market tightness. The ratio of openings to unemployed proxies wage-inflation pressure.
us_jolts.u: Labor market tight: wage-inflation worry lifts yields, pressuring high-P/E growth in Japan and supporting banks.
us_jolts.d: Openings falling: labor market softening and cuts pulled forward - relief for Japanese growth and rate-sensitive names.

us_umich.x: Consumer sentiment plus 1-year and 5-10 year inflation expectations. A jump in expectations is the signal the Fed dislikes most.
us_umich.u: Expectations spike: yields up, equities down - UW high-P/E growth in Japan.
us_umich.d: Expectations anchored: a relief signal that supports Japanese growth and duration-sensitive names.

us_claims.x: Every Thursday, the fastest data on the labor market. What matters is a change in the trend of the four-week moving average.
us_claims.u: Claims rising: labor softening and yields down; a spike becomes a recession trade. The firmer yen is a headwind for Japanese exporters.
us_claims.d: Claims falling: labor resilient and yields biased up. The softer yen supports Japanese exporters and banks.

us_eci.x: Quarterly wage and benefit costs. The Fed leans on it as the cleanest read on wage inflation because it strips out composition effects.
us_eci.u: Wage inflation sticky: cuts pushed back. UW high-P/E growth in Japan, OW banks.
us_eci.d: Wage growth cooling: soft-landing hopes support growth and quality in Japan.

us_housing.x: The thermometer for the most rate-sensitive sector of the US economy. Permits lead starts.
us_housing.u: Housing recovering: confirmation that lower rates are working. A tailwind for materials and housing-related names in Japan.
us_housing.d: Housing stalling: evidence that high rates are reaching the real economy. Negative read-across for Japanese cyclicals.

jp_boj.x: Eight meetings a year: the policy rate (currently 1.00%), the JGB purchase plan, the quarterly Outlook Report and the Governor's press conference. Hike expectations mean a stronger yen, stronger banks and weaker growth - the biggest macro event for Japanese equities.
jp_boj.u: Hawkish (a hike or a hike signal): yen up, JGB yields up. OW banks and insurers; UW exporters (autos, machinery), UW high-P/E growth, UW real estate.
jp_boj.d: Dovish (on hold with a cautious tone): yen down, yields down. OW exporters and real estate, UW banks.

jp_cpi.x: Core, ex-fresh food, is the benchmark. The distance from the BOJ's 2% target sets the pace of hikes, with the durability of services prices and wages the focus.
jp_cpi.u: Hot print: BOJ hike expectations build - yen up, OW banks, UW growth.
jp_cpi.d: Cooling: hikes pushed back - yen down, OW exporters.

jp_tokyo_cpi.x: Published at month-end as a one-month lead on the national CPI. The bond market trades it as a preview of the national print.
jp_tokyo_cpi.u: Upside: national CPI expected higher, yields up and yen firmer - banks over growth in Japan.
jp_tokyo_cpi.d: Cooling: hike expectations pared, yen softer - supports exporters and duration-sensitive names.

jp_tankan.x: The BOJ's quarterly business survey. The large-manufacturer DI is the headline, but for equities the capex plans and the assumed USDJPY rate matter most - the gap between corporate assumptions and spot is the room for earnings revisions.
jp_tankan.u: DI improving with confident capex plans: OW cyclicals. If spot is weaker than the assumed rate, exporters have room to revise guidance up.
jp_tankan.d: DI deteriorating: UW cyclicals, OW defensives.

jp_iip.x: Monthly manufacturing output, read together with the forecast index for the next two months. It captures semiconductor and auto production trends.
jp_iip.u: Output recovering: OW machinery, electronic components and autos.
jp_iip.d: Output being cut: the inventory cycle is deteriorating. UW cyclicals.

jp_machine.n: Core Machinery Orders (ex-ships and electric power)
jp_machine.x: Leads capex by six to nine months. Volatile, so read the three-month moving average. It maps directly onto machine-tool and factory-automation share prices.
jp_machine.u: Orders recovering: OW machinery and FA names such as Fanuc and SMC.

jp_trade.x: Export trends by region and product. The focus is exports to China and the volumes of semiconductor production equipment and autos.
jp_trade.u: Export volumes recovering: OW external-demand names.
jp_trade.d: Exports falling: external demand is stalling. Rotate into domestic demand and defensives.

jp_wages.x: Whether real wages stay positive is the condition for the wage-price virtuous circle, and therefore for the BOJ to keep hiking. The months when shunto results feed through, April to June, matter most.
jp_wages.u: Wages beat: BOJ hike expectations build - yen up, OW banks. With real wages positive, OW domestic consumption in retail and services.
jp_wages.d: Wages stalling: hikes pushed back and consumption in doubt. Yen softer, UW domestic consumer names.

jp_gdp.x: The consumption and capex components are the focus. Prone to revision, and less market-moving than CPI or a BOJ meeting.
jp_gdp.u: Growth beat: a tailwind for domestic-demand names and support for BOJ normalization.
jp_gdp.d: Negative growth: hike expectations pared and the yen softer, which helps exporters and leaves banks behind.

jp_watcher.x: The street-level economy as reported by taxi drivers, shop staff and the like. A monthly read on how inbound and domestic consumption actually feel.
jp_watcher.u: Sentiment improving: OW retail, restaurants and leisure.

ecb.x: Every six weeks: the deposit facility rate (currently 2.25%) and the Lagarde press conference. It reaches Japan through EUR/JPY and the profitability of exports to Europe.
ecb.u: Hawkish: euro up and European yields up. A weaker yen against the euro is a tailwind for Japan's exporters to Europe - autos and machinery.
ecb.d: Dovish: euro down, which erodes the margin on Japanese exports to Europe.

eu_hicp.x: The inflation print that drives ECB policy. Core and services prices are the focus.
eu_hicp.u: Upside: the ECB turns hawkish and the euro rises, supporting Japanese exporters to Europe.
eu_hicp.d: Cooling: cuts continue and the euro falls, squeezing Japanese export margins into Europe.

eu_pmi.x: The fastest sentiment read, out late in the month. German manufacturing PMI leads global capital-goods demand and correlates closely with Japan's machinery sector.
eu_pmi.u: Improving: OW Japanese capital goods sold into Europe - machinery and electricals.
eu_pmi.d: Deteriorating: UW Japanese names with high European exposure.

de_ifo.x: A survey of some 9,000 German firms. The expectations component carries the lead information.
de_ifo.u: Improving: European cyclicals recovering, which supports Japan's Europe-exposed cyclicals.
de_ifo.d: Deteriorating: the German manufacturing recession drags on - a headwind for Japanese machinery into Europe.

cn_pmi.x: The monthly thermometer for Chinese activity. The gap between NBS (large firms) and Caixin (smaller, export-oriented) is itself information. Japan's materials, construction machinery, machine tools and cosmetics are sensitive to Chinese demand.
cn_pmi.u: Back above 50: OW China plays such as Komatsu, Shiseido and materials, helped by the spillover from stronger HK/China equities.
cn_pmi.d: Below 50: UW China plays. Downward pressure on steel and chemical spreads.

cn_gdp.n: China GDP and Monthly Activity Data
cn_gdp.x: Industrial production, retail sales and fixed-asset investment are released with quarterly GDP. Whether property investment has bottomed is the central question.
cn_gdp.u: Activity improving: OW China plays and commodity-linked names such as copper and iron ore.
cn_gdp.d: Slowing: UW Japanese names with China exposure.

cn_credit.x: The aggregate measure of Chinese credit creation. The credit impulse leads Chinese activity and commodity markets by six to nine months.
cn_credit.u: Credit expanding: a bullish lead for commodities and for China-linked Japanese equities.
cn_credit.d: Credit contracting: a bearish lead for commodity-linked names.

cn_trade.x: A thermometer for world trade. Imports read on Chinese domestic demand, exports on global demand.
cn_trade.u: Imports recovering: a tailwind for Japanese companies exporting to China.
cn_trade.d: Imports falling: a headwind for Japanese materials and machinery with heavy China dependence.

opec.x: Decisions on output cuts and increases. Crude feeds through inflation into rates. Japan imports its oil, so a higher crude price is a terms-of-trade loss.
opec.u: Output cut (crude up): OW oil E&P such as INPEX, UW utilities, airlines and chemicals, with yields up via inflation.
opec.d: Output increase (crude down): a tailwind for import-dependent Japan. OW airlines, utilities and chemicals.

jackson.x: The late-August central bankers' symposium. Fed chairs have used the speech to pre-announce policy turns, which makes it the biggest event of the summer lull.
jackson.u: Hawkish message: yields up and equities down - OW banks, UW high-P/E growth in Japan.
jackson.d: Dovish message: easing hopes lift equities - OW Japanese growth and real estate.

us_treasury_ref.x: The Treasury's issuance plan. More long-end supply worsens the supply-demand balance, lifts the term premium and pushes long yields up - a headwind for equity valuations.
us_treasury_ref.u: Issuance raised: long yields up. UW high-P/E stocks in Japan, OW financials.
us_treasury_ref.d: Issuance restrained: relief on yields, which supports Japanese growth and REITs.

jp_jgb_auction.x: The size of the tail, the gap between average and lowest accepted price, measures demand. A weak super-long auction signals retreating life-insurer demand, and higher JGB long yields mean stronger banks and weaker property.
jp_jgb_auction.u: Weak auction (wider tail): yields up. OW banks, UW real estate and REITs.
jp_jgb_auction.d: Strong auction: yields down. OW real estate.

us_earnings_season.x: Results and AI capex guidance from AAPL, MSFT, NVDA and peers feed straight into the demand outlook for Japan's semiconductor production equipment and electronic component sectors.
us_earnings_season.u: AI capex raised: OW Tokyo Electron, Advantest, Lasertec and peers.
us_earnings_season.d: Capex cuts signaled: UW Japanese semiconductor names.

sox_events.n: Semiconductor Bellwethers (NVDA results / TSMC monthly sales)
sox_events.x: NVDA's results and TSMC's monthly revenue are the most important data on the semiconductor cycle, and the share-price driver for Japan's SPE, materials and power-semiconductor names.
sox_events.u: Upside surprise: OW the whole Japanese semiconductor chain.
sox_events.d: An inventory-correction signal: UW semiconductor production equipment.

jp_msci_rebal.x: Passive money mechanically buys additions and sells deletions. The name moves twice: on the announcement and on implementation, at the month-end rebalance close.
jp_msci_rebal.u: Addition: flow-driven buying into the implementation date.
jp_msci_rebal.d: Deletion: flow-driven selling. The move tends to reverse once the event has passed.

us_election.x: The direction of tariffs, tax and regulation changes. For Japan the focus is auto tariffs, defense spending and FX policy.
us_election.u: Tax cuts and deregulation expected: risk-on. A hard line on tariffs argues UW Japanese exporters, autos above all.
us_election.d: Tax rises and tighter regulation expected: risk-off, with Japanese high-beta cyclicals lagging.

jp_election.n: Japanese National Election / LDP Leadership Race
jp_election.x: Rates and the yen trade on fiscal expansion versus fiscal discipline. Aggressive fiscal policy tends to mean higher yields, a weaker yen and firmer domestic-demand equities.
jp_election.u: A pro-spending administration: OW domestic demand, construction and defense, with higher JGB yields putting banks on the OW side.
jp_election.d: A move toward austerity: UW domestic demand.
